books.title: After Christendom
books.subtitle: Faith after the church lost its cultural power
books.blurb: Essays on the end of cultural Christianity — the death of Christendom, the rise of the nones, the early church under Rome, and what a faithful, exiled church looks like now.

books.title: Born Again From Atheism
books.subtitle: How an Unbeliever Came to Faith, and What He Found There
books.blurb: James Bell was not a lapsed churchgoer who wandered back. He was an atheist with reasons, raised without a father, formed by Russell and the company of the clear-eyed, and he still respects the man who held those arguments. This is the whole account of what moved, slowly, against his preference, and what it cost. It takes the case for unbelief at full strength, keeps the wound and the argument distinct, and follows the erosion through Otto and Lewis and a night with no lightning in it, to a pulpit in Fenton, Michigan, and a table with five sons at it. Written toward the reader still on the other side, who should finish able to disagree, and unable to say he was handled.

books.title: Character Before Competence
books.subtitle: Leading the Church Without Losing Your Soul
books.blurb: The church keeps falling for the same lie, that a man who can do the work has therefore become the kind of man the work requires. This is a book about the difference, written by a working pastor who has stood on the wrong side of it. It traces the inner life of the leader from the qualifications God actually screens for to the day he hands the work to someone else, and it refuses, all the way through, to let the writer stand outside the indictment.

books.title: Come to the Table
books.subtitle: Disciple Making in Homes for Ordinary Christians
books.blurb: Jesus taught crowds, but he made disciples at tables. This book recovers his method for people with no title and no training: the meal, the text, the question, and the sending. By the last chapter you will have set your first table.

books.title: Common Grace
books.subtitle: What Pastors Learn When They Listen to the World
books.blurb: God did not lock his goodness inside the church. He scattered it across the whole field of human life — into the laboratory, the studio, the courtroom, the mouth of the honest unbeliever — and called it good before any of us got there. This is a book about the grace that is common: the kindness of God to people who do not yet know his name, and the slow, costly discipline of learning to recognize it without ever surrendering to it.

books.title: Dangerous Calling
books.subtitle: Why the Office of Pastor Is Not for Everyone
books.blurb: The office of pastor is not a career, a platform, or a reward for being good with words. It is a weight God lays on a particular kind of person and refuses to lay on most. This book argues, without softening the edge, that some should not enter the office, that the qualifications God screens for are matters of character before competence, and that the calling, when it is real, costs more than anyone tells you and is worth more than anything you gave up.

books.title: Deconstruction & Church Hurt
books.subtitle: Leaving, staying, and the wreckage in between
books.blurb: Essays for the wounded and the deconstructing — exvangelicals, purity culture, religious trauma, spiritual abuse, the prosperity gospel, and how consumerism and screens quietly form us.

books.title: Deep Roots
books.subtitle: Why Doctrine, Church History, and the Whole Story of Scripture Still Hold
books.blurb: James Bell takes the reader down to the roots of the Christian faith, the doctrines we recite without using, the councils we forgot we owe, and the single story Scripture has been telling all along. Written for skeptics, for Christians carrying real questions, and for anyone whose faith has outgrown the slogans it was handed, Deep Roots argues that the old depths are not a museum to admire but the only ground strong enough to stand on. It is theology that refuses to separate rigor from warmth, written from inside the room where people fall apart.

books.title: Earthen Vessels
books.subtitle: Why Our Bodies Matter to Our Faith
books.blurb: The church inherited a lie it never examined: that the soul is the real you and the body is the cage you carry it in. This book argues the opposite from the center of the faith — that God made matter, entered it, died in it, rose in it, and intends to redeem it. Your body is not the obstacle to your discipleship. It is the place your discipleship happens or does not happen at all.

books.title: Faithful in Exile
books.subtitle: Pastoral Leadership and the Church's Witness in a Post-Christian Age
books.blurb: The church in the West has lost the cultural power it held for sixteen centuries, and most of us are treating the loss like a catastrophe to be reversed. It isn't a catastrophe. It's a homecoming, a return to the church's oldest and most faithful condition, the condition of exile, where the people of God have always done their truest work. This book traces how Christendom rose and how it fell, and it argues that the long stretch of years in front of us is not a sentence. It's an assignment.

books.title: Hard Questions
books.subtitle: Honest answers for a skeptical age
books.blurb: Essays answering the questions people actually ask — suffering and evil, hell, miracles, science, the reliability of the Bible, the hiddenness of God, and whether faith is reasonable at all.

books.title: Justice & the Poor
books.subtitle: Mishpat, the poor at the gate, and the church's silence
books.blurb: Essays on biblical justice — mishpat and tsedaqah, the poor and the stranger, the immigrant and the refugee, jubilee and debt, and the eye of the needle.

books.title: Marriage: Communication & Conflict
books.subtitle: Fighting well, forgiving, and repairing what broke
books.blurb: Essays on the daily work of staying married — communication that works, fighting fair, forgiveness and repair, rebuilding trust, and the friendship a marriage can quietly lose.

books.title: Marriage: Covenant & Roles
books.subtitle: What marriage actually is, and how two people lead and serve
books.blurb: Essays on the shape of marriage — covenant rather than contract, one flesh, headship and submission read honestly, and two people learning to lead and serve each other.

books.title: Marriage: Crisis & Rebuilding
books.subtitle: Affairs, addiction, divorce, and starting again
books.blurb: Essays for marriages in the hardest places — affair recovery, addiction, mental health and depression, when divorce is faithful, second marriages, blended families, and a spouse who has lost faith.

books.title: Marriage: Money, Work & Seasons
books.subtitle: In-laws, work, kids, and the long seasons
books.blurb: Essays on the pressures that test a marriage over time — money, in-laws, the demands of work, the years after children, the empty nest, ministry, distance, and the men who quietly check out.

books.title: Marriage: Sex & Intimacy
books.subtitle: Intimacy as theology, honestly
books.blurb: Essays on sex and intimacy in a Christian marriage — intimacy as theology, and the honest conversation about the sexless marriage nobody names.

books.title: Mishpat
books.subtitle: God, the Poor, and the Justice the Church Forgot
books.blurb: Justice is not a partisan word smuggled into Scripture. It is one of the oldest words in Scripture, and the church has spent a long time learning not to hear it. This book recovers what the Bible means by mishpat and tsedaqah, traces God's relentless lean toward the poor and the foreigner, and refuses both the gospel that blesses your portfolio and the politics that swallows the gospel whole.

books.title: Necessary Words
books.subtitle: A Pastoral Theology of Courage and Difficult Conversations
books.blurb: The church has confused niceness with love and silence with peace, and the people who pay for it are the ones we refused to tell the truth. This is a book about the necessary word — the courage to confront sin, walk into conflict, and say the thing that wounds in order to heal. Speaking the truth in love is not a personality you were born with. It is an obedience, and most of us have spent our whole lives finding ways around it.

books.title: On Biblical Theology
books.subtitle: The whole Bible as one story that ends in Christ
books.blurb: Essays tracing the Bible as one story climaxing in Christ — the kingdom of God, exodus, the image of God, and living between the already and the not yet.

books.title: On Church History & Traditions
books.subtitle: The story you were born into
books.blurb: Essays on the church's long memory — the councils and creeds, how Christianity became an empire and then became American, the mystics, and what the great traditions can teach each other.

books.title: On Core Doctrine
books.subtitle: The great truths, explained without condescension
books.blurb: Essays on the doctrines the church confesses — the Trinity, the gospel, grace, the reliability of Scripture, hell, and what Calvinists and Arminians are actually arguing about.

books.title: On Faith & Doubt
books.subtitle: Living honestly with the questions
books.blurb: Essays for the doubting — doubt as a spiritual practice, living with permanent uncertainty, the dark night, and keeping the question inside the faith instead of leaving to keep it.

books.title: On Manhood
books.subtitle: Anger, provision, and being a man who stays
books.blurb: Essays on manhood from a man raised without a father and raising five sons — anger, provision, presence, crisis, and the men the church forgot to form.

books.title: On Money & Stewardship
books.subtitle: Debt, generosity, and what Jesus meant by mammon
books.blurb: Essays on money — debt, generosity, wealth, tithing, contentment, and what Jesus actually meant when he said you cannot serve God and mammon.

books.title: On Prayer
books.subtitle: How to pray when you do not feel like it
books.blurb: Essays on prayer — praying when the feeling does not come, the Lord's Prayer, confession, the tired person's prayer, and the prayer you cannot finish.

books.title: On Rest & Sabbath
books.subtitle: Silence, waiting, and a life that can be sustained
books.blurb: Essays on rest — the sabbath you keep skipping, resting in a culture of exhaustion, silence, solitude, waiting, and the long obedience of ordinary faithfulness.

books.title: On Womanhood
books.subtitle: Identity, calling, and worth beyond the roles
books.blurb: Essays on womanhood — identity, calling, motherhood, and worth that does not depend on a role or a season.

books.title: On Work & Vocation
books.subtitle: Calling and the God of the ordinary job
books.blurb: Essays on work as calling — vocation, career, ambition, entrepreneurship, faith at a job nobody shares, and the sacredness of ordinary labor.

books.title: One Body, Many Churches
books.subtitle: A Theology of Unity for a Fractured Church
books.blurb: The church Jesus prayed for is one. The church the world sees is splintered into thousands of pieces, each certain it holds the center. This book holds two truths the modern church keeps tearing apart: that the body of Christ is genuinely one, and that the differences between churches are genuinely real. It refuses the two cheap exits of sectarian pride and mushy relativism, and it asks the harder question instead: what would it cost you to give the dying Christ the one thing He asked for?

books.title: Parenting the Hard Places
books.subtitle: Prodigals, doubt, screens, and the crises nobody prepped you for
books.blurb: Essays for the hardest parts of parenting — the prodigal, the child who doubts or walks away or comes out, special needs, single parenting, screens and phones, sex and identity, and grief.

books.title: Parenting: Ages & Stages
books.subtitle: What each season of childhood actually needs
books.blurb: Essays on raising children stage by stage — toddlers, the elementary years, the middle-school wilderness, teenagers, and the young adult who leaves, with the spiritual milestones to aim for at each age.

books.title: Parenting: Discipline & Character
books.subtitle: Forming the heart, not just the behavior
books.blurb: Essays on discipline and character — forming the heart rather than the behavior, letting children fail, raising the resilient and the unimpressive, and resisting the idol of the well-rounded child.

books.title: Preach the Word
books.subtitle: The Primacy of Expository Preaching in the Local Church
books.blurb: The pulpit has become a stage, and the sermon a performance measured by how well it moves a room. This book argues that the preacher's only authority is the text in front of him, that exposition is not a method among methods but the recovery of a church that has stopped expecting God to speak. It is written for the pastor who is tired of being interesting and wants, again, to be faithful.

books.title: Preaching & Leading the Church
books.subtitle: The pulpit, the staff, and the revitalized church
books.blurb: Essays on leading the church — preaching, staff and elders and deacons, church revitalization and planting, and the budget as a theology.

books.title: Race & the Church
books.subtitle: The most segregated hour, honestly examined
books.blurb: Essays on race and the church — the image of God against the lie of race, the black church, white evangelicalism, the most segregated hour, and what reconciliation actually requires.

books.title: Raising Kids in the Faith
books.subtitle: Handing on a faith worth keeping
books.blurb: Essays on forming faith at home — teaching children to pray and read the Bible, raising kids who question rather than perform, family rhythms, and finding a church that will not wound them.

books.title: Sent Into the City
books.subtitle: The Church's Calling to Its Neighborhood and World
books.blurb: The church was never gathered to be hidden. It was gathered to be sent into the actual street, the actual block, the actual city where God has placed it. This is a book about trading the machinery of programs for the slow obedience of presence, about loving the people you did not choose, and about what it costs to seek the welfare of a place you might rather leave.

books.title: The Captive Church
books.subtitle: Nationalism, Empire, and the Cost of Cultural Christianity
books.blurb: The church keeps reaching for the kingdoms of the world on the terms the world offers them, and keeps calling the reach faithfulness. This book follows the one temptation Jesus refused in the wilderness through Constantine, the denarius, the flag on the platform, and the water we no longer see, and it indicts every tribe by the same cross. It is not a book about politics. It is a book about who the church belongs to.

books.title: The Church & the Nation
books.subtitle: Faith after the flag
books.blurb: Essays on the church's captivity to the nation — Christian nationalism, flags in the sanctuary, render unto Caesar, the religious right, and loving a country without worshiping it.

books.title: The Church's Reckonings
books.subtitle: Abuse, mental health, and the questions the church avoids
books.blurb: Essays on the reckonings the church cannot avoid — the sexual abuse crisis, mental health handled badly, women in ministry, lament, and the prophets who made everyone uncomfortable.

books.title: The First Flock
books.subtitle: The Church's Calling to Care for Pastors and Their Families
books.blurb: The man you call to feed you is starving, and you have not noticed. This is a book about the duty a congregation owes the shepherd it ordained to shepherd it, and about the first flock no one counts, the family inside the parsonage who absorb the cost of a ministry they never chose. It is written to the church as much as to the pastor, because the pastor cannot fix this alone, and the church has been pretending it is not the one holding the knife.

books.title: The God Who Is Not Nice
books.subtitle: Recovering the Holy God a Therapeutic Church Traded Away
books.blurb: The functioning god of much of the American church is warm, agreeable, and reliably on our side, and he cannot save anyone. James Bell, who came to faith from a settled atheism and did not leave unbelief for a god that small, traces the sentimental deity to his birth records, the five-article creed Christian Smith and Melinda Lundquist Denton named in 2005 and the therapeutic turn Philip Rieff saw coming in 1966, and then walks the reader back into the text, to the burning bush, the shaking doorposts of Isaiah 6, the terrified boat on Galilee, and Bonhoeffer's war on cheap grace. Written by a pastor who preached the nice god because it filled rooms, and stopped. The holy God is not safe. He was never nice. He is good, and he is the only comfort that holds.

books.title: The Hidden Life of a Pastor
books.subtitle: Tending Your Soul While Tending the Flock
books.blurb: The most dangerous thing in ministry is not failure. It is a public life that has quietly outrun the private communion that was supposed to feed it. This is a book about the hidden life with God — the only thing that finally sustains the visible one — written for the shepherd who has not yet admitted how thirsty he has become.

books.title: The Pruning
books.subtitle: Church Decline, Faithful Endurance, and the Promise of Renewal
books.blurb: The numbers are real, and they are not lying to us. But the question the church keeps asking — are we dying? — is the wrong question, because it assumes the only two states are health and death. There is a third thing, and the Vinedresser has done it before. This is a book about the difference between the church being killed and the church being cut, and why the second one looks almost exactly like the first while it is happening.

books.title: The Undershepherd
books.subtitle: Pastoral Leadership, Authority, and the Care of God's People
books.blurb: The pastor is not the shepherd. He is an under-shepherd, holding a borrowed staff over a flock that was never his, answerable to the One whose blood bought them. This book refuses the two cheap roads of domination and abandonment, and argues that the only authority worth having in the church is the kind that bleeds for the sheep instead of feeding on them.

books.title: The Undivided Life
books.subtitle: Following Jesus Through an Ordinary Week
books.blurb: Most of us were handed a faith for Sundays and a calendar for the other six days, and we have lived in the gap ever since. This is a book about closing it. Marriage and money, work and rest, the body and the home and the friends who know your real name, all of it claimed by one Lord and offered as one life.

books.title: The Unfinished Church
books.subtitle: Calling, Vision, and the Future God Is Building
books.blurb: The church is not a monument to defend or a method to chase. It is a building still rising, founded on a promise older than any of us and aimed at a city we have not yet seen. This book is about what it means to belong to something God is building and we are not finishing.

books.title: To the Ends of the Earth
books.subtitle: Global Mission, National Partnership, and the Sent Church
books.blurb: The center of Christianity no longer sits where the maps of our missionary fathers drew it; it has moved south and east, and most Western churches never noticed they were left holding a parochialism they mistook for the faith itself. This book argues that the Great Commission is non-negotiable and that the way we have often carried it out is indictable, and that the only path forward is partnership that surrenders control to the very churches the West once condescended to. It is a call to become again what the church has always been underneath its committees and budgets: a sent people, going to the ends of the earth and paying for it.
